name: DeepGEMM
works_with: NVIDIA SM90 or SM100 GPUs with PyTorch
short: DeepSeek's library of fast GPU kernels for the matrix maths inside large language models.
what: A CUDA kernel library from DeepSeek for the core maths of modern LLMs: FP8, FP4 and BF16 matrix multiplies, fused mixture-of-experts with overlapped communication (Mega MoE), and scoring kernels for DeepSeek's lightning indexer. Kernels compile at runtime, so installing needs no CUDA compilation. DeepSeek also pitches it as a readable resource for learning GPU kernel optimization.
who: Engineers who build LLM training or inference systems on NVIDIA SM90 or SM100 GPUs. If you don't write GPU code, skip it.
needs: An NVIDIA GPU with SM90 or SM100 architecture
Compilers and standard libraries with C++20 `<format>` support
CUDA Toolkit 12.9 or higher and PyTorch 2.3 or higher
CUTLASS 4.0 or higher (cloned with the Git submodule)

steps.title: Clone with submodules and build for development
steps.text: The README has you print each script with `cat` before running it.
steps.code:
# Submodule must be cloned
git clone --recursive git@github.com:deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM.git
cd DeepGEMM

# Link some essential includes and build the C++ extension
cat develop.sh
./develop.sh

steps.title: Use it from Python
steps.text: Import `deep_gemm` in your project. The `tests` folder has worked examples.

try.label: From the README
try.text:
import deep_gemm

Then call fp8_gemm_nt for a basic FP8 GEMM (D = C + A @ B.T). See tests/test_mega_moe.py and tests/test_attention.py for fuller examples.

watch: You handle input transposition and FP8 casting yourself. The README says its simple PyTorch helpers for these may be slower.
Mega MoE needs a multi-process launch with symmetric memory and PyTorch 2.9 or later.
SM90 and SM100 need scaling factors in different formats (FP32 on SM90, packed UE8M0 on SM100).
DeepSeek has a separate DeepGEMM-Ascend repo for Ascend hardware.
